chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Jarir al-Qummi who said:
I asked al-Reza (peace be upon him) about feathers — are they ritually pure (from a slaughtered animal)? So he said: My father (peace be upon him) used to stuff his pillow with feathers.

key_terms.الريش: Feathers; here specifically referring to bird feathers used for stuffing pillows
key_terms.ذكي: Ritually pure/slaughtered; from tadhkiyah, the Islamic method of ritual slaughter that renders meat and by-products halal and tahir
key_terms.يَتَوَسَّد: To use as a pillow, to lay one's head upon; here indicating stuffing a pillow with feathers

ai.seo_question: Are bird feathers ritually pure (tahir) according to Imam al-Reza?
ai.summary: Abu Jarir al-Qummi asked Imam al-Reza (AS) whether feathers (from birds) are considered ritually pure, implying they come from a properly slaughtered animal. The Imam answered indirectly by citing his father's practice of using feathers as pillow stuffing, thereby indicating their permissibility through Imamic precedent. In Shia jurisprudence, the purity of feathers depends on whether the bird was ritually slaughtered; this hadith uses the Imams' personal practice as a legal indicator (seerah al-ma'sumeen).
word_analysis: used to use as a pillow/stuff a pillow with
